goal: Make the DB the sole store with a unified data model. Loading becomes SQL-ranked retrieval. Synthesis writes structured CRUD ops directly to the DB. Session context persists between sessions. Memory capture is frictionless via MCP tools. A web frontend replaces markdown files for human inspection.
architecture: Five phases: (A) Unified schema migration — data_points table replaces chunks+nodes, edges gains reason column, vec_data replaces vec_chunks, v2-to-v3 migration. (B) MCP server — persistent Python process exposing search_memories, write_memory, delete_memory, traverse_graph tools via mcp SDK. (C) DB-primary synthesis — MEMORY_OPS-only output, no PROJECT blocks or markdown writing, salience scores from LLM, provenance edges. (D) Web frontend — Python HTTP server + single HTML page with vis.js graph visualization, browse/search/edit/delete. (E) Integration — smart SQL loading in load_memory.py, session continuity via SessionEnd context writing, install.py MCP registration, skill deprecation, dead code removal, end-to-end tests.
tech_stack: Python 3.9+, SQLite WAL mode, sqlite-vec, mcp Python SDK, FastEmbed, pytest, http.server, vis.js, vanilla JS/HTML/CSS

phases.name: Unified Schema Migration (v2 to v3)
phases.rationale: The data_points table is the foundation everything else depends on. MCP server (B), synthesis (C), web frontend (D), and integration (E) all query data_points. Migration must be complete and verified before any consumer can be built.

tasks.name: Define v3 schema DDL and DataPointRow dataclass
tasks.done_when: storage.py has SCHEMA_V3_DDL constant with data_points table (id, type, name, content, scope, entry_type, source_type, source_sessions, created_at, salience, access_count, last_accessed, evidence_count, consolidated, content_hash, simhash, entities, properties), VEC_DATA_DDL for vec_data virtual table (embedding float[384], +data_point_id TEXT, +type TEXT), and all required indexes. DataPointRow dataclass defined with all fields. SCHEMA_VERSION NOT bumped yet (A3 handles that after migration logic exists). Tests verify: schema DDL creates tables without error, DataPointRow round-trips through insert/query.

tasks.name: Implement data_points CRUD helpers
tasks.verification: python3 -m pytest tests/test_storage.py -v -k 'insert_data_point or query_data_point or update_data_point'
tasks.done_when: storage.py exports: insert_data_point(conn, dp) returns ID; query_data_points_by_scope(conn, scope, type, min_salience) with optional filters; query_data_point_by_id(conn, id); update_data_point_salience(conn, id, salience); update_data_point_content(conn, id, content, entities); soft_delete_data_point(conn, id) sets salience=0. All auto-generate id and content_hash. Tests cover: insert+query round-trip, scope filtering, type filtering, salience floor filtering, soft delete sets salience=0, missing ID returns None.

tasks.name: Implement v2-to-v3 data migration
tasks.done_when: storage.py has _migrate_v2_to_v3(conn) function that: (1) creates data_points table, (2) copies chunks rows to data_points with type='memory' preserving IDs, (3) copies nodes rows to data_points with type='entity' preserving IDs, (4) ALTERs edges table to add reason column, (5) creates vec_data table and copies vec_chunks data mapping chunk_id to data_point_id, (6) drops old chunks/nodes/vec_chunks tables, (7) runs post-migration integrity check (all edge source/target IDs exist in data_points). _migrate_schema() dispatches v2->v3. Tests verify: chunks become type='memory' data_points with same IDs, nodes become type='entity' data_points with same IDs, edges remain valid (source/target reference data_points), vec_data has correct data_point_id references, integrity check passes, idempotent when run twice.

tasks.name: Migrate profile sections to data_points with type='profile'
tasks.done_when: _migrate_v2_to_v3 also parses global-long-term-memory.md for profile sections (About Me, Current Projects, Technical Environment, Patterns & Preferences), creates data_points with type='profile', scope='user', salience=1.0, consolidated=1 for each section. Content is the full section text. Tests verify: profile sections extracted, type/scope/salience/consolidated set correctly, sections with no content are skipped, idempotent (content_hash dedup).

tasks.name: Update embeddings.py for vec_data table
tasks.done_when: embeddings.py updated: VEC_CHUNKS_DDL replaced by VEC_DATA_DDL, ensure_vec_table creates vec_data, index_chunks renamed to index_data_points (operates on data_points table), search_similar queries vec_data joining data_points instead of chunks, ScoredChunk renamed to ScoredDataPoint holding DataPointRow. Backward-compatible: if vec_chunks table exists (pre-migration), operations are no-ops with warning. All existing embedding tests updated and passing.

tasks.name: Archive markdown files and verify full migration
tasks.done_when: Migration function moves daily/*.md, global-long-term-memory.md, and project-memory/*.md to ~/.claude/memory/.archive/ with timestamp suffix. Only runs after data_points migration succeeds (guard: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM data_points must be > 0). Tests verify: files moved to .archive/, .archive/ directory created, guard prevents archival if data_points is empty, original files no longer exist after archival.

phases.name: MCP Server
phases.rationale: The MCP server gives Claude native tool access to the memory DB. It depends on the v3 schema (data_points, vec_data, edges) being in place. Independent of synthesis (C) and web frontend (D) — those can develop in parallel once schema is stable.

tasks.name: Create MCP server scaffold with mcp SDK
tasks.done_when: scripts/memory_server.py exists with: mcp SDK Server instance, stdio transport setup, FastEmbed model loading in background thread, graceful startup (responds within 10 seconds), DB connection via storage.ensure_db(). Registers 4 tool stubs (search_memories, write_memory, delete_memory, traverse_graph) that return placeholder responses. Tests verify: server instantiates without error, tool names registered, FastEmbed loads in background (mocked), DB connection established.

tasks.name: Implement search_memories tool
tasks.done_when: search_memories(query, scope?, top_k?) embeds query via embed_text(), runs KNN search on vec_data, applies composite scoring from score_memory() (0.50 vec_sim + 0.25 recency + 0.25 salience), applies graph boost (+0.05 per edge connection in top-K set, capped at +0.15), returns ranked results with IDs, content, score, entities, and provenance chain edges. Fallback: if FastEmbed unavailable, returns SQL-only results (salience + recency ranked). Tests verify: vector search path (mocked embeddings), SQL fallback path, graph boost applied, scope filtering, top_k limiting, result format includes IDs and provenance.

tasks.name: Implement write_memory tool
tasks.done_when: write_memory(fact, scope, salience?, entities?, supersedes?, relation_type?, relation_reason?) atomically: inserts data_point with type='memory', generates embedding and inserts to vec_data, creates/upserts entity data_points for each entity in entities list, creates 'mentions' edges from memory to each entity, creates optional provenance edge (supersedes/refines/contradicts/etc) if supersedes parameter provided. scope='user' auto-sets salience=1.0 and consolidated=1. Tests verify: data_point created, embedding indexed, entities created as data_points, mentions edges created, provenance edge created with reason, user scope auto-pins, atomic rollback on failure.

tasks.name: Implement delete_memory tool
tasks.done_when: delete_memory(id, reason?) soft-deletes: sets salience=0 on target data_point, invalidates related edges (valid_to=now), creates a deletion marker data_point (type='memory', content=reason, salience=0) with a 'supersedes' edge from marker to deleted data_point — preserving provenance. Returns confirmation with deleted data_point content for Claude's context. Tests verify: salience set to 0, edges invalidated, deletion marker created, supersedes edge created, reason preserved, non-existent ID returns error.

tasks.name: Implement traverse_graph tool
tasks.done_when: traverse_graph(entity, depth?, relationship_type?) walks the knowledge graph from a data_point using recursive CTE. Follows both entity edges AND memory provenance chains. Returns connected data_points with their relationship types, distances, and content. Optional depth limit (default 2), optional relationship_type filter. Tests verify: single-hop traversal, multi-hop traversal (depth=2), relationship_type filtering, provenance chain following, empty graph returns empty result, respects depth limit.

tasks.name: Add pip dependency for mcp SDK
tasks.done_when: pyproject.toml has mcp SDK in dependencies (or optional-dependencies group). pip install -e . installs the mcp package. Import succeeds.

phases.name: DB-Primary Synthesis
phases.rationale: Synthesis must write to data_points (not markdown). Depends on the v3 schema (Phase A) but is independent of MCP server (B) and web frontend (D). This is the core pipeline change that eliminates dual write paths.

tasks.name: Rewrite synthesis prompt for MEMORY_OPS-only output
tasks.done_when: _build_synthesis_instructions() rewritten to request ONLY ===MEMORY_OPS=== JSON output — no ===PROJECT:=== blocks. Format: {"ops": [{"action": "ADD", "fact": "...", "scope": "...", "type": "...", "salience": 0.8, "entities": [...], "supersedes": "dp_id", "reason": "..."}]}. Salience is LLM-assigned (0.0-1.0). Instructions explain salience spectrum (0.3-0.5 transient, 0.7-0.9 important, 1.0 permanent). Three scopes documented: user, global, {project}. Tests verify: prompt contains MEMORY_OPS format, no PROJECT block references, salience guidance present, three scopes documented.

tasks.name: Update MEMORY_OPS parser for enhanced format
tasks.done_when: MemoryOp dataclass gains salience (float, optional) field. parse_synthesis_output() handles MEMORY_OPS-only output (no PROJECT blocks required). When output contains ONLY ===MEMORY_OPS===...===END===, parses successfully. Backward-compatible: mixed PROJECT+MEMORY_OPS still works. Tests verify: MEMORY_OPS-only parsing, salience field extracted, backward compat with mixed format, malformed JSON warning.

tasks.name: Rewrite apply pipeline for DB-only writes
tasks.done_when: New apply_memory_ops_v3(conn, ops) function: ADD inserts data_point (type='memory') with LLM-assigned salience, generates embedding, creates entity data_points + mentions edges; UPDATE modifies data_point content/entities/salience; DELETE soft-deletes (salience=0) with provenance edge; NOOP increments evidence_count. No markdown writing anywhere. No call to build_dailies_from_project_blocks, write_daily_files, append_to_ltm, or mark_routed_entries. Tests verify: ADD creates data_point with correct type/scope/salience/entities, UPDATE modifies existing, DELETE creates provenance edge, embedding generated for ADD/UPDATE, no filesystem writes.

tasks.name: Create provenance edge helpers
tasks.done_when: storage.py exports: create_provenance_edge(conn, source_id, target_id, edge_type, reason) for supersedes/contradicts/led_to/refines/supports edges; query_provenance_chain(conn, data_point_id) returns ordered chain of supersession/contradiction edges leading to/from a data_point using recursive CTE. Tests verify: each edge type created correctly, provenance chain follows multi-hop supersession (A supersedes B supersedes C), chain is ordered newest-first, empty chain for data_point with no provenance.

tasks.name: Update synthesis_cron.py for v3 pipeline
tasks.done_when: synthesis_cron.py calls apply_memory_ops_v3 instead of apply_results when v3 schema detected. Pre-retrieval uses data_points table (not chunks). Session context data_point written after synthesis completes (type='session_context', scope=project, content=summary of work done). Tests verify: v3 path invoked when SCHEMA_VERSION=3, session_context data_point created, pre-retrieval queries data_points, backward compat (v2 schema still calls old apply path).

tasks.name: Write session_context data_points in synthesis
tasks.done_when: After synthesis completes, synthesis_cron creates a session_context data_point per project with: type='session_context', scope=project name, salience=0.8, content=summary of what was worked on (extracted from transcript topics), properties JSON with session_id and files_touched (if available). Creates context_for edges to entity data_points mentioned in the session. Optional continues edge to previous session_context for same project. Tests verify: session_context created with correct fields, context_for edges to entities, continues edge to prior context, properties includes session metadata.

phases.name: Web Frontend
phases.rationale: The web frontend queries data_points for browse/search/edit. Depends on v3 schema (Phase A) but is independent of MCP server (B) and synthesis (C). Uses only standard library + vis.js CDN — no build step.

tasks.name: Create HTTP server with API endpoints
tasks.done_when: scripts/web_app.py has a Python HTTP server (http.server based) binding to 127.0.0.1:8742 (fallback 8743-8749 on port conflict). API endpoints: GET /api/stats (memory count, salience distribution, recent activity), GET /api/data_points (filter by scope/type/salience/date, paginated), GET /api/search?q=query (keyword + optional semantic search), GET /api/graph?scope=X (nodes + edges for vis.js), GET /api/data_point/:id (single data_point with edges). CSRF token generated at startup, required for write operations. Tests verify: each endpoint returns correct JSON shape, scope/type filtering works, pagination parameters honored, CSRF token validated on writes, server binds to localhost only.

tasks.name: Create write/delete API endpoints
tasks.done_when: POST /api/data_point/:id (edit memory content/salience/scope) and DELETE /api/data_point/:id (soft delete with reason). Both require CSRF token. Edit updates content + content_hash + re-embeds. Delete sets salience=0, invalidates edges, creates deletion marker. Tests verify: edit updates content, re-embedding triggered, delete soft-deletes, CSRF required and validated, missing ID returns 404.

tasks.name: Create single-page HTML frontend with vis.js
tasks.verification: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; html = Path('templates/web/index.html').read_text(); assert 'vis-network' in html; assert 'csrf' in html.lower(); print('OK')"
tasks.done_when: templates/web/index.html is a self-contained single HTML file with inline CSS and vanilla JS. Loads vis.js from CDN. Views: Dashboard (stats, salience histogram, recent activity), Browse (filter by scope/type/salience/date), Search (keyword input with results list), Graph (interactive vis.js network), Memory Detail (single data_point with edges and provenance chain), Edit/Delete (forms with CSRF token). CSRF token embedded by server at page serve time. web_app.py serves index.html at GET / with token injection.

tasks.name: Add web_app.py to install.py
tasks.done_when: install.py links web_app.py in link_scripts(). templates/web/ directory copied in copy_templates(). Success message updated to mention 'python3 ~/.claude/scripts/web_app.py' for web UI.

phases.name: Integration: Smart Loading, Session Continuity, and Deprecation
phases.rationale: Integration wires together the schema (A), MCP server (B), and synthesis (C). Smart loading replaces firehose markdown loading with SQL queries. Session continuity reads session_context at startup. install.py registers the MCP server. Skills are deprecated. Dead code is removed. This must be last because it depends on all three prior phases. Web frontend (D) is not a dependency — it can ship independently.

tasks.name: Rewrite load_memory.py for SQL-ranked retrieval
tasks.done_when: main() in load_memory.py replaces markdown file loading with 5 SQL queries against data_points: (1) user profile (scope='user', salience>0.5, ~500 tokens), (2) session continuity (type='session_context', most recent for project, ~500 tokens), (3) project memories (scope=project, type='memory', salience>0.4, top 20, ~2K tokens), (4) global knowledge (scope='global', type='memory', salience>0.6, top 10, ~1K tokens), (5) recent activity (created_at > 3 days ago, top 15, ~2K tokens). Deduplication: running seen_ids set excludes duplicates across queries. Access tracking: batch_update_access on all served data_point IDs. Total budget ~6K tokens. Tests verify: each query tier returns correct data_points, dedup across tiers, access tracking fires, token budget respected, graceful fallback if DB missing.

tasks.name: Add session continuity to SessionStart output
tasks.done_when:
When the most recent session_context data_point exists for the current project scope, load_memory.py outputs a 'Session Continuity' section showing what was last worked on, which entities were involved (from context_for edges), and status (from properties JSON). Format: '## Last Session
You were working on: [content]
Entities: [list]
Status: [status]'. Tests verify: session continuity section appears when context exists, absent when no context, correct entity extraction from edges, properties.status displayed.
